title: Doña Juana la Loca (Joanna the Mad)
source: Museo del Prado, Madrid, P04584 (public domain). Wikimedia Commons: Doña Juana "la Loca" (Pradilla).jpg (3051 x 2088 px). Not the Buenos Aires or other copies.
caption: She won't let them bury him. #spanishhistory #prado #pradilla #lovestory #storytime
_verify: VERIFIED, Wikipedia EN (Doña Joanna the Mad): 1877, Prado; Joanna watches over the coffin of Philip I, who died suddenly; she stands upright, empty expression, hands clenched; courtiers look bored and tired; said to carry the coffin with her, believing he would wake; medal of honour at the 1878 National Exhibition in Madrid. Prado easy-read page: winter landscape at dusk; coffin moved from Burgos to Granada; they stopped at a convent, Joanna thought it was friars, it was nuns, so she refused to stay and took the coffin into the countryside; court rests by a bonfire, faces show boredom and compassion; a monk prays in front of her, a woman looks at her.
GENERAL HISTORY (low risk): Philip died in 1506 aged 28; Joanna was confined at Tordesillas for decades, by her father and later her son.
CAUTIOUS: jealousy as the reason for leaving the convent is phrased 'it is said' (slide 5).

slides.headline: She won't let them bury him.
Castile, 1506
slides.text: Castile, 1506. King Philip the Handsome dies suddenly, at just 28. His wife, Queen Joanna, will not let him rest.

slides.headline: The coffin
slides.text: She has his coffin carried across Spain, from Burgos to Granada, in the middle of winter. The whole court must follow.

slides.headline: The queen
slides.text: Here they stop in an open field. Joanna stands in black, perfectly still, eyes fixed on the coffin, hands clenched.

slides.headline: The convent
slides.text: There was a convent nearby, but it belonged to nuns. Joanna refused to stay. It is said she would let no woman near him.

slides.headline: The court
slides.text: So her courtiers huddle by a fire in the cold, exhausted and bored. Some look at her with pity. How many more nights?

slides.headline: The prayer
slides.text: A monk prays in front of her. A lady watches her face. People whispered that she believed her husband would wake up.

slides.headline: Mad?
slides.text: Was she mad, or a widow whose grief no one understood? Her father, then her son, kept her locked away for decades.

slides.headline: Love or madness
slides.text: Pradilla's painting won the top medal in Madrid in 1878 and made her story famous. Was it love, or madness?
